title: BPW-2026-0588
text:
[JOINT REPORT(S)]
BPW-2026-0588
BOS + BCA
CD ALL
CONSIDERATION OF CEQA ADDENDUM NO. 5 – RECYCLA PROGRAM
Recommending the Board:
FIND, based on the independent judgment of the decision-maker, after consideration of the whole of the administrative record, including the Environmental Impact Report for the Citywide Exclusive Solid Waste Collection and Handling system (SCH #2013021052), certified on April 8, 2014 (2013 PEIR) and Addendum No. 5 to the 2013 PEIR dated October 19, 2026; and pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Sections 15162 and 15164 and Addendum No. 5, dated October 19, 2026, that no major revisions to the 2013 PEIR are required and no subsequent EIR, or negative declaration is required for approval of the project, as amended by Addendum 5;
APPROVE and forward this report with transmittals to the Mayor and City Council with the request that the Board of Public Works be authorized to award and execute exclusive franchise contracts for the collection and handling of solid resources from commercial establishments and applicable multifamily properties in specified zones under the recycLA program with:
Table 1 - Recommended Awards for Exclusive Franchise Zone Contracts
Large zones
Small zones
Arakelian Enterprises, Inc. (dba Athens
Services) – West Los Angeles, North Central, Harbor Zones
NASA Services, Inc. – Downtown Zone
Consolidated Disposal Service, LLC (dba Republic Services) – Northeast Valley, South Los Angeles Zones
Ware Disposal, Inc. – Southeast Los Angeles, East Downtown Zone
Universal Waste Systems, Inc – Noreast Zone
Large Zones
Small Zones
USA Waste of California, Inc. (dba Waste Management) – West Valley, Southeast Valley Zones
FIND that the recommended awards are in the best interests of the City and will support the continued provision of reliable, environmentally responsible, and cost-effective solid resources collection services to commercial establishments and applicable multifamily properties;
UPON the Mayor’s and Council’s authorization, the President or two members of the Board will execute the contracts; and
DIRECT the Bureau of Sanitation to oversee the seamless transition from the existing recycLA agreements to the recycLA 2.0 agreements and to provide coordinated outreach and assistance to affected customers before and during implementation.
(W.O.: S16QS025)
